body.p: In the Office Action mailed on May 22, 2024, claims 1-16 are pending in the application; Claims 1-7 and 11-12 are withdrawn; Claims 8-10 and 13-16 stand rejected. Claims 8 and 16 are amended herein.
As set forth herein, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections and objections of the claims is respectfully requested.

Claims 8-10 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention. The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.
Claims 8 and 16 are amended as suggested by the Examiner. Therefore, this rejection should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claims 8-10 and 13-15 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over US Patent Publication No. 2006/0201432 (hereinafter referred as Pratt) in view of US Patent Publication No. 2007/0106179 (hereinafter referred as Bagha); in view of US Patent Publication No. 2006/0243280) (hereinafter referred as Caro) further in view of US Patent Publication No. 2006/0206013) (hereinafter referred as Rothman). The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

With respect to the newly cited Caro reference, it is disagreed that this reference teaches an algorithm. Furthermore, it is disagreed that even if Caro teaches an algorithm, the inputs to any mathematical calculation requires both active and passive auscultation to obtain a diagnosis. Paragraph [0091] clearly explains that combined "multiplexing" lung indicators from both types of auscultation is required. The present invention only uses passive auscultation as that term is defined in Caro. See paragraph [0078] for the Caro definition of passive auscultation. See paragraph [0025] of Caro for the Caro definition of active auscultation. The active auscultation requires the introduction of an audible signal into the body of the examined patient and thereafter
receiving and monitoring the signal after it has passed through the body. Caro absolutely requires the combination of both passive and active auscultation in order to make any diagnosis.

Regarding the failure of Caro to teach an algorithm, there are an exhaustive number of mathematical expressions that are disclosed however none of these are algorithms that are used with digital sound data to plot resulting data as calculated in a frequency domain where amplitudes of frequencies differentiate between categories of sounds corresponding to various levels of respiratory disease. Further, there is no actual first data set that can be identified in Caro. The Examiner references paragraph [0091] however this paragraph simply recites the "multiplexing" of lung condition indicators obtained from both active and passive auscultation. Multiplexing is a process to consolidate multiple signals into a single composite signal. Caro teaches away from any type of signal analysis that only uses passive auscultation. The entire disclosure of Caro is directed to pointing out the shortcomings of passive auscultation and the need to multiplex signals in order to obtain effective medical treatment.

With respect to the Examiner's reliance on Figures 3A-3D of Caro, these figures are derived indicators associated with active auscultation., i.e., sounds associated with signals obtained by monitoring the introduction of external audible signals that have passed through the body, not the natural sounds that are generated by an animal in passive auscultation. These figures therefore have no relevant teaching or meaning as compared to the presently claimed invention which is limited to passive auscultation, as this term is defined in Caro.

With respect to the Rothman reference, it is not disagreed that Rothman provides a health score indication but it is disagreed that there is any reasonable teaching to combine Rothman and Caro. Rothman is used within the context of improving patient care at a hospital by receiving incoming medical data, applying an algorithm, and then generating the health score. The type of medical data is derived from a large combination of factors including pain assessment, blood pressure, respiration rate, body temperature, heart patterns, and others. Accordingly, the health score is generated by a large number of factors that have no relationship or bearing on a targeted respiratory condition. The combination of Rothman and Caro requires one to ignore the basic purpose of Rothman as teaching a general health condition for purposes of hospital care for humans and to replace that purpose with a specific respiratory condition of a non-human such as cattle. It is asserted that one seeking a solution for determining respiratory conditions for non-human animals would seek a solution for such in a patent reference that teaches a scoring system for human patients in a hospital setting.
Therefore, this rejection should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claim 16 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over US Patent Publication No. 2006/0201432 (hereinafter referred as Pratt) in view of US Patent Publication No. 2007/0106179 (hereinafter referred as Bagha); in view of US Patent No. 6,699,204) (hereinafter referred as Kehyayan); in view of US Patent Publication No. 2006/0243280) (hereinafter referred as Caro) further in view of US Patent Publication No. 2006/0206013) (hereinafter referred as Rothman). The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Claim 16 should be considered allowable at least for the same reasons set forth above with respect to the deficiencies in both the Caro and Rothman references. Accordingly, this rejection should also be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Based on the foregoing, Applicant believes all pending claims are in condition for allowance and such disposition is respectfully requested.
